target_customer: Knowledge workers and teams, about 70% with corporate emails at launch, who type repetitive text in Gmail, CRMs and web apps
problem: People retype the same messages and make mistakes; Text Blaze lets them insert snippets with shortcuts, forms and formulas.
business_model: Freemium Chrome extension with paid individual and business plans
product_category: Text expansion and snippets, later AI prompt templates

founders.name: Dan Barak
founders.background_notes: Co-founder quoted in TechCrunch; no background published there.

founders.name: Scott Fortmann-Roe
founders.background_notes: Listed on YC page; no background in opened sources.

technical_complexity.rationale: A browser extension with templating and form fields is standard engineering; the hard parts are reliability across web apps.

defensibility.rationale: Users' saved snippets and shared team libraries create some lock-in, but text expansion tools are easy to copy.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copy was found by 2026; sibling products AI Blaze and Data Blaze were added.

market_need_then: At launch in 2021 the Chrome extension had over 70,000 users, about 70% with corporate emails, and early revenue, showing organic demand.

branding.domain_note: Product runs on blaze.today; company is Blaze Today Inc.

identity.logo: Flame-style product mark per Chrome Web Store
identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, productivity-focused with claims such as 'eliminate repetitive typing and mistakes'

branding.brand_signature: Blaze family of products: Text Blaze, AI Blaze, Data Blaze
branding.community_and_virality: Active community forum at community.blaze.today; 1,900+ Chrome Web Store reviews averaging five stars (company claim).

brand_strength.rationale: Memorable name, five-star store reviews and an active community forum support word-of-mouth growth, though there is no independent brand press.

outcome_analysis: Text Blaze grew through a free Chrome extension with product-led distribution, reaching 70,000 users before its $3.3M seed in 2021 and a claimed 800,000 users later. A four-person team was the plan at seed, suggesting capital efficiency. It remains independent and has extended into AI Blaze and Data Blaze.
notes: Seedtable lists a $125k pre-seed and CB Insights $3.43M over four rounds; only the $3.3M seed is confirmed by TechCrunch. Competitor search found only later vendor comparison pages (TextExpander, Magical, 2024 era), none dated near the batch, and TechCrunch compared Text Blaze to Zapier, Grammarly and Copy.ai only as analogies, so the list is empty. Founder roles and backgrounds not found; a startup profile (not opened) lists Dan Barak as CEO.
